intro: Hi! I'm going to ask about 15 short questions in four rounds so I can set up your own assistant. Every question has a suggested answer: just say 'ok' to take it, or tell me what you want instead. You can skip any question. At the end I show you everything I'm about to create and wait for your yes.

questions.text: In a sentence or two: who are you and what do you do (student, job, projects)?
What do you most want an assistant to help with over the next month?
questions.default: keeping track of deadlines and notes

questions.text: Which of these do you already use? (Obsidian, Discord, Google Calendar, Gmail, a school portal, none)
Where should your assistant's folder go? (a folder path; it will hold the boot file and a vault folder of notes, which is the assistant's memory)

rounds.title: Round 3 of 4: how it should behave

questions.text: What should the assistant be called?
How should it talk to you?
What may it do on its own, without asking?
questions.default: read and write notes in the vault, run scripts in the project folder, run tests, search the web for information

questions.text: What must it ask you about first?
questions.default: anything that sends a message, email or post to another person; anything that costs money; deleting files; changing system settings
touch payments or banking, share passwords or keys, lend or use the user's accounts when they are not present

rounds.title: Round 4 of 4: what to watch, and limits

questions.text: What should it keep an eye on? (deadlines, a school portal, email, your PC's health, nothing yet)
When should it stay quiet (no pings)?
Which plan do you use for the AI?
Do you want a private chat channel (a Discord DM) to talk to it from your phone?

map.friend: talk like a chill friend: plain casual sentences, short, no bullet lists unless asked for a list, real reactions allowed; competent and direct underneath. Reply to technical work with one casual sentence first, then the substance.
map.professional: talk like a calm professional assistant: clear, polite, complete sentences, no slang; short paragraphs; lists only when the content is a list.
map.direct: talk in short direct lines: answer first, then the reason in one line; no filler, no small talk unless the user starts it.

map.claude_pro: The plan has limits that reset every 5 hours and weekly. Do cheap work first: search before reading, read only the part needed, keep sessions lean, and say plainly when usage looks tight. Send routine writing and code jobs to a free or cheap model when one is set up, and review the result yourself.
map.claude_max: The plan has higher limits that still reset every 5 hours and weekly. Keep sessions lean, avoid idle loops, and say plainly when weekly usage looks tight. Send routine writing and code jobs to a free or cheap model when one is set up, and review the result yourself.
map.api_credit: Every call costs real money. Keep a small spend cap, prefer the cheapest model that does the job, never loop without a stop rule, and report spend when asked.
map.unsure: The plan and its limits are not known yet. Keep sessions lean, avoid idle loops, and ask the user to check their usage page when a long task is planned.

map.yes: A private Discord DM channel will be set up as an add-on. Until then, answer in the terminal. Every reply to the user goes out deliberately; text typed in the terminal is not sent anywhere else.
map.later: No chat channel yet. Answer in the terminal. When the user wants a private chat channel, walk them through it step by step as an add-on.
